title: 2.7.3 Individual PA Part 3: Find and Fix
description: Four bugs in one program. Run it, read what happens, fix each one, and name what kind of bug it was. Fixed, the program runs top to bottom and prints a correct receipt.

steps.title: Press Run first
steps.instructions: Do not change anything yet — just press **Run**. One of the four bugs stops the whole file before a single line runs, and the console tells you exactly which line it gave up on. That is where you start.

steps.title: Fix one, Run, repeat
steps.instructions: After **every** fix, press **Run** again. Two of the four bugs never print an error message: one prints a number that is wrong, and one makes the console go quiet until the run is stopped. Compare what you get with what it should say.

steps.title: Say what kind each one was
steps.instructions:
Above each fix, add a comment naming the kind: **syntax**, **runtime** or **logic**.

* **syntax** — the file is not valid JavaScript, so nothing runs.
* **runtime** — it is valid, it starts, and then it stops with an error.
* **logic** — it runs all the way through and prints something untrue.
hints: The kind is about WHEN it goes wrong, not about how hard it was to find
Two of these four are the same kind as each other

requirements.title: Bug 1 — nothing runs at all
requirements.description: The console names the line it gave up on. Help: 1.5.38 (Reading an Error Message)
requirements.hint: Go to the line the console named and count the quote marks on it. One string needs two. Close it, then press Run.

requirements.title: Bug 2 — it stops part way through
requirements.description: A name is used that was never declared. Help: 1.5.39 (Cause a ReferenceError on Purpose)
requirements.hint: The console prints the exact word it could not find. Spell it the way the line above spelled it, then press Run — the next line may have been waiting behind this one.

requirements.title: Bug 3 — the receipt says Savings: 30
requirements.description: It should say Savings: 40. Help: 2.4.13 (Skipping a Round with continue)
requirements.hint: `continue` jumps straight to the next round, so anything written after it is skipped on the rounds that take it — and week 3 takes it. Put the line that has to happen every week above the `continue`, then press Run.

requirements.title: Bug 4 — the receipt prints, then the console goes quiet
requirements.description: The walking log never prints a line and the run is stopped. It should print Week 1, Week 3 and Week 5. Help: 2.4.16 (The continue Trap in a while Loop)
requirements.hint: In a while loop, `continue` jumps back to the condition — past the line that moves the counter. So the counter never changes and the loop asks the same question forever. Put the line that moves it above the `continue`, then press Run.

requirements.title: All four bugs are named
requirements.description: A comment beside each fix names its kind: syntax, runtime or logic. Help: 1.5.38 (Reading an Error Message)
requirements.hint: Four fixes, four comments. The three words to use are syntax, runtime and logic.
